title: Correcting a learned physical invariant improves world-model rollouts
abstract: arXiv:2608.23526v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: World models can predict video without learning dynamics that they reliably preserve. We test whether a frozen DreamerV3 trained only on pendulum video learns a scalar that its own latent transition treats as approximately conserved. A label-free search recovers the same energy-like invariant across independently trained conservative models, while the same procedure finds no comparable invariant in matched damped models. During autonomous rollouts, this quantity drifts. Projecting the latent state back toward its initial level set reduces rollout error in all three conservative models, whereas matched random constraints usually increase it. These results distinguish a dynamically meaningful invariant from a merely decodable correlate and reveal a concrete failure mode: a world model can learn a physical constraint from pixels yet violate that constraint when it imagines forward.

translated_title: 修正学习到的物理不变量可改善世界模型推演
translated_abstract: 世界模型可以在不学习可靠保持的动态特性的情况下预测视频。我们测试了一个仅在钟摆视频上训练的冻结DreamerV3是否学习到一个其自身潜在转换近似守恒的标量。无标签搜索在独立训练的保守模型中恢复了相同的能量类不变量，而相同程序在匹配的阻尼模型中未发现类似不变量。在自主推演过程中，该量发生漂移。将潜在状态投影回其初始水平集可减少所有三个保守模型中的推演误差，而匹配的随机约束通常会增加误差。这些结果区分了具有动态意义的不变量与仅可解码的相关性，并揭示了一个具体失败模式：世界模型可以从像素中学习物理约束，但在想象未来时却违反该约束。
tldr: 本文发现世界模型能从像素中学习物理不变量，但自主推演时会违反该约束，通过将潜在状态投影回初始水平集可显著减少推演误差。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that world models can learn physical invariants from pixels but violate them during rollouts, and projecting latent states back to their initial level set significantly reduces rollout errors.
